source_text: Ἵνα δὲ μὴ δοκῶμεν ἀπὸ λέξεως Ἑβραϊκῆς τοῖς μὴ καταλαμβάνουσι, πότερον συγκαταθετέον αὐτῇ ἢ μὴ, φέρειν παραμυθίαν περὶ τοῦ προφήτην εἰρηκέναι ἐκ παρθένου τεχθήσεσθαι τοῦτον, ἐφ᾿ οὗ τῇ γενέσει λέλεκται τὸ „μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν ὁ θεὸς“, φέρε ἐπ᾿ αὐτῆς τῆς λέξεως παραμυθησώμεθα τὸ λεγόμενον. ὁ μὲν κύριος ἀναγέγραπται εἰρηκέναι τῷ Ἄχαζ· „αἴτησαι σεαυτῷ σημεῖον παρὰ κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ σου εἰς βάθος ἢ εἰς ὕψος,“ ἑξῆς δὲ τὸ διδόμενον σημεῖον τὸ „ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει καὶ τέξεται υἱόν.“ ποῖον οὖν σημεῖον τὸ νεάνιδα, μὴ παρθένον τεκεῖν; καὶ τίνι μᾶλλον ἁρμόζει γεννῆσαι „Ἐμμανουὴλ,“ τουτέστι „μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν ὁ θεὸς,“ ἆρα γυναικὶ συνουσιασθείσῃ καὶ διὰ πάθους γυναικείου συλλαβούσῃ ἢ ἔτι καθαρᾷ καὶ ἁγνῇ καὶ παρθένῳ; ταύτῃ γὰρ πρέπει γεννᾶν γέννημα, ἐφ᾿ ᾧ τεχθέντι λέγεται τὸ „μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν ὁ θεός.“ ἐὰν δὲ καὶ οὕτως εὑρεσιλογῇ λέγων ὅτι τῷ Ἄχαζ εἴρηται· „αἴτησαι σεαυτῷ σημεῖον παρὰ κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ σου,“ ἀπαντήσομεν· κατὰ τοὺς χρόνους τοῦ Ἄχαζ τίς ἐγεννήθη, ἐφ᾿ οἷ τῇ γενέσει λέγεται τὸ „Ἐμμανουὴλ, ὅ ἐστι μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν ὁ θεός,·“ εἰ γὰρ οὐδεὶς εὑρεθήσεται, δηλονότι τὸ τῷ Ἄχαζ εἰρημένον τῷ οἴκῳ εἴρηται Δαυὶδ διὰ τὸ „ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυὶδ“ ἀναγεγράφθαι τὸν σωτῆρα γεγονέναι „τὸ κατὰ σάρκα“· ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ „σημεῖον“ τοῦτο „εἰς βάθος ἢ εἰς ὕψος“ λέγεται εἶναι, ἐπεὶ „ὁ καταβὰς οὗτός ἐστι καὶ ὁ ἀναβὰς ὑπεράνω πάντων τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἵνα πληρώσῃ τὰ πάντα.“ ταῦτα δὲ λέγω ὡς πρὸς τὸν Ἰουδαῖον συγκατατιθέμενον τῇ προφητείᾳ. λεγέτω δὲ καὶ Κέλσος ἤ τις τῶν σὺν αὐτῷ, ποίῳ νῷ ὁ προφήτης περὶ μελλόντων ἢ ταῦτα ἢ ἕτερα λέγει, ὁπόσα ἀναγέγραπται ἐν ταῖς προφητείαις· ἆρα γὰρ προγνωστικῷ μελλόντων ἢ οὔ; εἰ μὲν γὰρ προγνωστικῷ μελλόντων, θεῖον εἶχον πνεῦμα οἱ προφῆται· εἰ δ᾿ οὐ προγνωστικῷ μελλόντων, παραστησάτω τὸν νοῦν τοῦ ἀποτολμῶντος καὶ λέγοντος περὶ μελλόντων καὶ θαυμαζομένου παρὰ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ἐπὶ προφητείᾳ.
pass_a_gloss: So that we may not seem to be bringing consolation from Hebrew language to those who do not understand, whether to agree with it or not, let us bring consolation about the prophet having said that this one will be born from a virgin, on which the generation is said to be 'God with us', let us be consoled by the word itself. The Lord is written to have said to Ahaz, 'Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God, either into depth or into height', and next the sign being given is 'Behold, the virgin will have in womb and will bear a son'. What kind of sign is it for a young woman, not a virgin, to give birth? And to whom does it more suit to bear 'Emmanuel', that is 'God with us', to a woman who has had intercourse and has conceived through female passion, or to one who is still pure and holy and a virgin? For it is fitting for her to bear offspring, on which it is said 'God with us'. But if someone were to rationalize saying that it was said to Ahaz, 'Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God', we will respond, according to the times of Ahaz, who was born, on which the generation is said to be 'Emmanuel, which is God with us'? For if no one is found, it is clear that what was said to Ahaz was said to the house of David, because the savior is written to have been born 'according to the flesh' from the seed of David. And also this 'sign' is said to be 'into depth or into height', since 'he who descended is also he who ascended above all the heavens, so that he might fill all things'. I say these things as to a Jew who agrees with the prophecy. Let Celsus or anyone with him say, with what mind does the prophet speak about future things, either these or others, as many as are written in the prophecies, does he have a mind that knows future things or not? For if he has a mind that knows future things, the prophets had a divine spirit, if not, let him present the mind of the one who dares and speaks about future things and is admired by the Jews for prophecy.

Behold, the virgin will have in womb and will bear a son
he who descended is also he who ascended above all the heavens

pass_b_english: Lest we appear to be offering consolation drawn from the Hebrew tongue to those who do not grasp it — whether they agree with it or not — let us instead find our comfort in the very wording of the prophecy: that the prophet said this one would be born of a virgin, and that on his birth the name 'God with us' is bestowed (Isaiah 7:14). Scripture records that the Lord said to Ahaz, 'Ask a sign for yourself from the Lord your God, whether in the depth or in the height' (Isaiah 7:11), and the sign given immediately follows: 'Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son.' What sort of sign would it be for a young woman, not a virgin, to give birth? And to whom does it more fittingly belong to bear 'Emmanuel' — that is, 'God with us' — a woman who has known intercourse and conceived through human passion, or one who remains pure, holy, and a virgin? For it is fitting for such a one to bear the offspring upon whose birth the words 'God with us' are declared. But if someone tries to rationalize by insisting the promise was spoken to Ahaz — 'Ask a sign for yourself from the Lord your God' — we will answer: in the days of Ahaz, who was born, upon whose birth the name 'Emmanuel, which is God with us,' is pronounced? If no one is found, then clearly what was said to Ahaz was addressed to the house of David, because the Savior is written to have been born 'according to the flesh' from the seed of David (Isaiah 7:14). Moreover, this 'sign' is said to reach 'into depth or into height,' since 'he who descended is also he who ascended above all the heavens, that he might fill all things' (Ephesians 4:10). I speak these things as one addressing a Jew who accepts the prophecy. Let Celsus, or anyone allied with him, declare: with what mind does the prophet speak of future things — whether these or others recorded in the prophecies? Is it a foreknowing mind, or not? For if it is a foreknowing mind, the prophets possessed a divine spirit; if not, let him explain the mind of the one who dares to speak of the future and is admired among the Jews for prophecy.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the distinction between 'young woman' (νεάνιδα) and 'virgin' (παρθένος), and the causal/conditional structures. Scripture citations in Pass B (Isaiah 7:14, Isaiah 7:11, Ephesians 4:10) correctly identify the biblical loci for the quoted/alluded Greek phrases. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source.

greek/origen_celsum.xml: "παρθένος" translated as "virgin"; "ἐμμανουὴλ" translated as "Emmanuel"; "μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν ὁ θεός" translated as "God with us"; "προφήτης" translated as "prophet"; "προγνωστικῷ" translated as "knowing future things"; Pass B includes correct citations: Isaiah 7:11, Isaiah 7:14, Ephesians 4:10.
